Chapter 9: The Ongoing Battle — Resistance Never Sleeps
You know, just when you think you’ve finally beaten resistance, it has a way of sneaking back in—sometimes even stronger than before. The truth is, resistance never really disappears. It just changes tactics, showing up in new forms to chip away at your confidence and throw you off track.
Over time, creators learn to expect its return. They start to spot its different disguises and, instead of panicking, they meet it with a little more patience and determination.
Let me share a story. Imagine a novelist who’s just published a big hit. Suddenly, she’s paralyzed—feeling the weight of repeating her success. Those old doubts slip back in, only now they’re wearing new outfits: What if the next book doesn’t measure up? What if the critics were right all along?
It’s so tempting to back away, to play it safe. But she remembers what got her here: showing up every day, trusting the process, and focusing on the work—not the outcome.
Here’s something most people miss—resistance is actually a sign of growth. The more meaningful your work, the stronger the pushback. It’s almost as if resistance is testing you, whispering, “How much do you really want this? Will you keep going, even when it’s tough?”
After a while, the creator starts to see resistance not as an enemy, but almost like an old companion. It’s a reminder that the work matters, and that something important is on the line. The battle is ongoing, yes—but that battle is proof you’re moving forward.
Of course, there are days when resistance wins. The work doesn’t get done. Doubt feels overwhelming. But here’s where the real growth happens—the creator forgives these setbacks, comes back to the practice, and starts again. It’s not about perfection. It’s about persistence.
And as time goes on, the relationship with resistance changes. It’s not so scary anymore. It loses its grip. The creator learns to work with it, maybe even use it as fuel instead of letting it stand in the way.
That ongoing war of art? It never truly ends. But with every small victory, every time you push through, the next battle gets just a little bit easier.
